summary: Backend regression + fix-verification for task-assignment email dispatch (iter99). 9/9 pytest tests passed, BUT direct DB inspection revealed a CRITICAL bug in the fix: emails are still NOT being sent for real users. The recipient lookup in create_notification() only queries db.users (which is EMPTY — 0 docs), while actual task assignees live in db.team_users (17 docs). The fire-and-forget email path short-circuits at the user lookup, so no Resend call is ever made in production.

critical.issue: Recipient lookup uses db.users.find_one(...) but real assignees are stored in db.team_users (and db.admins). db.users collection has 0 documents in this environment. Result: emails NEVER dispatch — the original user-reported bug is NOT actually fixed for the common case (assigning tasks to team users). In-app notification insert succeeds, but the httpx call to https://api.resend.com/emails is silently skipped because `user` is None.

action_items: URGENT: In /app/backend/routes/inapp_notifications.py :: create_notification(), replace `await db.users.find_one(...)` with a lookup that checks BOTH db.team_users and db.admins (mirror the pattern used by _user_exists() in routes/tasks.py). Example: `user = await db.team_users.find_one({'id': user_id}, {...}) or await db.admins.find_one({'id': user_id}, {...}) or await db.users.find_one(...)`.

After fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_task_email_iter99.py and add an assertion (or a log line inside create_notification like `logger.info('[task-email] queued to %s', to_email)`) so the dispatch is externally observable — right now there's no positive log on success, only on failure, making regression testing hard.
Consider adding a temporary INFO log inside _send_task_email() before the httpx.post() so future tests / on-call can verify dispatch without waiting for a Resend bounce.
critical_code_review_comments: Wrong collection queried for recipient email (see critical issue above) — root cause of the still-broken email flow.
No positive-path logging: only failure path emits a log line. Add a debug/info log at task-queue time so the fire-and-forget dispatch is observable in production.
APP_BASE_URL default 'https://oll.co' — verify this is intended for production CTA links; if the deployed frontend URL differs, users will hit the marketing site instead of the app.

_send_task_email swallows all exceptions with a warning. Consider surfacing 4xx from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain) at WARNING level with response body so ops can act — right now the string form of the exception may be empty for non-raising httpx responses.

success_rate.backend: 100% (test suite) — but underlying feature is BROKEN due to collection mismatch

seed_data_creation: Created 1 test task 'TEST_iter99 email <hex>' assigned to team_user Anushree Sharma (id bb047704-...); notification doc landed in notifications_inapp. Task was deleted after test. RESEND_API_KEY already set in /app/backend/.env — no seeding needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The pytest suite (test_task_email_iter99.py) is green because it only asserts that (a) task creation returns 200, (b) no [task-email] failed log appears (which is trivially true when the dispatch is skipped), and (c) self-notifications are correctly skipped. The real bug — that db.users is queried instead of db.team_users/db.admins — was found by direct DB inspection. Once the main agent fixes the collection lookup, rerun this file and additionally verify via backend logs that _send_task_email() is being invoked (currently no success log exists; ask main agent to add `logger.info('[task-email] queued to %s', to_email)` before the httpx.post call for observability). All 4 notification CRUD endpoints (GET, unread-count, PATCH read, POST read-all) and both LMS smoke endpoints (GET /api/lms/all-schools, PATCH /api/schools/{id}/link-lms) passed regression.

rca of the issue.symptom: User reports emails are NOT being sent on task assignment even after the reported fix.
rca of the issue.reproduction: 1) Login as admin@oll.co. 2) POST /api/tasks with assigned_to=<team_user_id>. 3) Inspect notifications_inapp collection — doc IS inserted. 4) Inspect backend logs and Resend dashboard — NO email dispatched. 5) Direct DB query: db.users.count_documents({}) == 0, db.team_users.count_documents({}) == 17.
rca of the issue.root_cause: create_notification() in routes/inapp_notifications.py, line 117-120, does `db.users.find_one({'$or': [{'id': user_id}, {'user_id': user_id}]}, ...)`. The `users` collection is empty in this deployment — all human accounts are stored in `team_users` and `admins`. The `if user and user.get('email')` guard therefore always fails and the asyncio.create_task(_send_task_email(...)) line is never reached.
rca of the issue.mitigation: Change the recipient lookup to a multi-collection resolver mirroring _user_exists() in routes/tasks.py — check team_users first, then admins, then users as fallback. Preserve the projection of {_id:0, email:1, name:1, full_name:1}.
